2	# LLM Wiki
3	
4	A pattern for building personal knowledge bases using LLMs.
5	
6	This is an idea file, it is designed to be copy pasted to your own LLM Agent (e.g. OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode / Pi, or etc.). Its goal is to communicate the high level idea, but your agent will build out the specifics in collaboration with you.
7	
8	## The core idea
9	
10	Most people's experience with LLMs and documents looks like RAG: you upload a collection of files, the LLM retrieves relevant chunks at query time, and generates an answer. This works, but the LLM is rediscovering knowledge from scratch on every question. There's no accumulation. Ask a subtle question that requires synthesizing five documents, and the LLM has to find and piece together the relevant fragments every time. Nothing is built up. NotebookLM, ChatGPT file uploads, and most RAG systems work this way.
11	
12	The idea here is different. Instead of just retrieving from raw documents at query time, the LLM **incrementally builds and maintains a persistent wiki** — a structured, interlinked collection of markdown files that sits between you and the raw sources. When you add a new source, the LLM doesn't just index it for later retrieval. It reads it, extracts the key information, and integrates it into the existing wiki — updating entity pages, revising topic summaries, noting where new data contradicts old claims, strengthening or challenging the evolving synthesis. The knowledge is compiled once and then *kept current*, not re-derived on every query.
13	
14	This is the key difference: **the wiki is a persistent, compounding artifact.** The cross-references are already there. The contradictions have already been flagged. The synthesis already reflects everything you've read. The wiki keeps getting richer with every source you add and every question you ask.
15	
16	You never (or rarely) write the wiki yourself — the LLM writes and maintains all of it. You're in charge of sourcing, exploration, and asking the right questions. The LLM does all the grunt work — the summarizing, cross-referencing, filing, and bookkeeping that makes a knowledge base actually useful over time. In practice, I have the LLM agent open on one side and Obsidian open on the other. The LLM makes edits based on our conversation, and I browse the results in real time — following links, checking the graph view, reading the updated pages. Obsidian is the IDE; the LLM is the programmer; the wiki is the codebase.
17	
18	This can apply to a lot of different contexts. A few examples:
19	
20	- **Personal**: tracking your own goals, health, psychology, self-improvement — filing journal entries, articles, podcast notes, and building up a structured picture of yourself over time.
21	- **Research**: going deep on a topic over weeks or months — reading papers, articles, reports, and incrementally building a comprehensive wiki with an evolving thesis.
22	- **Reading a book**: filing each chapter as you go, building out pages for characters, themes, plot threads, and how they connect. By the end you have a rich companion wiki. Think of fan wikis like [Tolkien Gateway](https://tolkiengateway.net/wiki/Main_Page) — thousands of interlinked pages covering characters, places, events, languages, built by a community of volunteers over years. You could build something like that personally as you read, with the LLM doing all the cross-referencing and maintenance.
23	- **Business/team**: an internal wiki maintained by LLMs, fed by Slack threads, meeting transcripts, project documents, customer calls. Possibly with humans in the loop reviewing updates. The wiki stays current because the LLM does the maintenance that no one on the team wants to do.
24	- **Competitive analysis, due diligence, trip planning, course notes, hobby deep-dives** — anything where you're accumulating knowledge over time and want it organized rather than scattered.
25	
26	## Architecture
27	
28	There are three layers:
29	
30	**Raw sources** — your curated collection of source documents. Articles, papers, images, data files. These are immutable — the LLM reads from them but never modifies them. This is your source of truth.

1	# AI 生态技术栈全景——从 LLM 到应用的完整链路
2	
3	> 综合 `AI基本知识.md` 的内容，梳理大模型生态中核心概念的分层关系与协同逻辑。
4	
5	## 一句话全景
6	
7	> 开发者通过 **Prompt Engineering** 指导 **Agent（智能体）** 运作；Agent 遇到专业知识时，利用 **Embedding** 技术去 **向量数据库** 中通过 **RAG** 检索资料；遇到需要执行的操作，通过 **MCP 协议** 调用外部工具；而如果基础模型在特定领域表现不够专业，还可以通过 **Fine-tuning** 对其进行深度改造。**整个工作流程由 Harness Engineering 管理、测试和保障。**
8	
9	## 四层架构
10	
11	```
12	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
13	│            Harness Engineering                   │
14	│    （安全管控 · 状态管理 · 执行沙箱 · 回退）       │
15	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
16	│                   AI Agent                       │
17	│    （感知 → 规划 → 执行 → 反思）                  │
18	├──────────────┬──────────────────┬───────────────┤
19	│     RAG      │       MCP       │   Prompt       │
20	│  (知识检索)   │    (工具调用)    │  (指令控制)    │
21	├───────┬──────┴──────┬───────────┴───────┬───────┤
22	│Embed  │  Vector DB  │  Fine-tuning      │  LLM  │
23	│(向量化)│  (向量存储)  │  (模型定制)       │ (引擎)│
24	└───────┴─────────────┴───────────────────┴───────┘
25	```
26	
27	## 概念关系图谱
28	
29	| 层级 | 概念 | 核心问题 | 类比 |
30	|------|------|---------|------|
31	| **引擎层** | [[wiki/concepts/llm\|LLM]] | 通用智能从哪里来？ | 发动机 |
32	| **控制层** | [[wiki/concepts/prompt-engineering\|Prompt Engineering]] | 如何让引擎做特定的事？ | 方向盘 |
33	| **代理层** | [[wiki/concepts/ai-agent\|AI Agent]] | 如何让 AI 自主完成任务？ | 驾驶员 |
34	| **知识层** | [[wiki/concepts/rag\|RAG]] | 知识不够/过时怎么办？ | 地图 |
35	| **工具层** | [[wiki/concepts/mcp\|MCP 协议]] | 如何操作外部系统？ | 手脚 |
36	| **数据层** | [[wiki/concepts/embedding\|Embedding]] | 如何让计算机理解语义？ | 翻译器 |
37	| **存储层** | [[wiki/concepts/vector-database\|向量数据库]] | 海量语义如何高效检索？ | 图书馆 |
38	| **定制层** | [[wiki/concepts/fine-tuning\|Fine-tuning]] | 通用模型不够专精怎么办？ | 进修 |
39	| **保障层** | [[wiki/concepts/harness-engineering\|Harness Engineering]] | 如何确保安全可靠？ | 安全笼 |
40	| **局限层** | [[wiki/concepts/幻觉-hallucination\|AI 幻觉]] | 为什么会出错？ | 固有特性 |
41	
42	## 关键洞察
43	
44	### 1. RAG vs Fine-tuning：何时用哪个？
45	
46	| 维度 | RAG | Fine-tuning |
47	|------|-----|-------------|
48	| 是否改变模型 | 否 | 是（改权重）|
49	| 更新知识 | 即时（换文档即可） | 慢（需重新训练）|
50	| 适合场景 | 事实查询、企业知识库 | 格式控制、风格固定、专业能力 |
51	| 成本 | 低 | 高 |
52	| **建议** | **能 RAG 就先 RAG，不够再微调** |
53	
54	### 2. RAG vs MCP：两种扩展的分工
55	
56	这两个概念最容易混淆。关键区别：
57	- **RAG** 是"读"——从外部获取**知识**（文档、数据库记录），扩充 LLM 的上下文
58	- **MCP** 是"写"——执行**操作**（发消息、更新数据库、运行代码），扩展 LLM 的行动能力
59	
60	### 3. AI 幻觉的双面性
61	
62	虽然工程上 RAG 是用来抑制幻觉的，但在创意领域（写作、头脑风暴、游戏设计），"幻觉"本质上就是**想象力**。看场景决定是抑制还是利用。
63	
64	## 引申思考
65	
66	1. 当前这 10 个概念中，哪些会随着技术发展而消失？哪些是永久的？
67	   - MCP 可能会被更好的标准取代
68	   - Prompt Engineering 可能随着模型理解能力的提升而变得不重要
69	   - **LLM、Agent、RAG** 这三个概念很可能长期存在
70	
71	2. 对于知识库构建者来说，RAG 和 LLM Wiki（[[karpathy的wiki方法论]]）是两种不同的范式：
72	   - RAG：运行时检索，不维护持久结构
73	   - LLM Wiki：构建时编译，维护持久结构
74	   - 两者可以互补——Wiki 作为"半结构化知识层"，RAG 作为"实时检索层"
